question: How does a remote client establish a bounded identity before requesting Essays capabilities?
selected_option: Explicit owner-approved device pairing registers one asymmetric client key, then short-lived audience- and scope-restricted sender-constrained access tokens use DPoP proofs, rotating refresh credentials, expiry, and revocation.
rationale: The user explicitly selected OPT-AUTH-PAIRING-DPOP after the gate presented pairing plus DPoP, OIDC plus PKCE and DPoP, and mutual-TLS alternatives. Pairing keeps the first local-first vertical independent of an external identity provider while retaining per-device proof and selective revocation.

required_semantics: pairing is visible to the owner, requires an explicit owner confirmation, is single-use, and expires
each client generates and retains its own asymmetric private key; the private key never leaves that client
issued access tokens are short-lived, audience-restricted, resource-restricted, scope-restricted, and sender-constrained to the paired public key
every protected request carries a DPoP proof bound to the HTTP method and target URI with a unique identifier and bounded clock window
the verifier rejects proof replay, key mismatch, expired tokens, wrong audience, wrong resource, wrong method, wrong URI, and insufficient scope
refresh credentials rotate, reuse is detected, and device credentials can expire, be revoked, and be replaced through an owner-visible recovery path
pairing, token validity, and DPoP proof establish client authentication only; every Essays command still requires capability, expected-revision, idempotency, policy, and effect checks
authentication decisions and outcomes produce redacted evidence without persisting private keys, bearer material, pairing secrets, or reusable proofs
non_implications: pairing does not grant editorial, workspace, agent, browser, publication, or external-effect authority
a valid token or DPoP proof does not bypass semantic command validation or explicit effect authorization
this selection does not choose cryptographic libraries, key storage, token formats, endpoint paths, deployment topology, or public exposure
this selection does not satisfy the Essays security-owner gate or prove protocol security, implementation conformance, release, or deployment

remaining_blockers: Essays security-owner review of the remote authentication binding
remote capability authorization and grant semantics
Product Capability decision and dependent contracts
authored ontology closure and DomainSpec generation
deferred_decisions: Cryptographic crates, platform key stores, token representation, nonce challenges, endpoint paths, recovery UX, and deployment configuration are later implementation and security bindings.
